The primary goal of social distancing is to slow down the outbreak of COVID-19, reducing the chance of infection among high-risk populations and decreasing the burden on healthcare systems [4]. This concept is often referred to as "flattening the curve," which means preventing surges in illness that could overwhelm healthcare systems [4]. Social distancing works by breaking or slowing the chain of transmission from person to person. People can spread the coronavirus for at least five days before showing symptoms, so social distancing limits the number of people an infected person comes into contact with before they realize they have the virus [4]. This is crucial because, without a way to make people better once they fall sick or make them less contagious, slowing or stopping the spread of the virus is the only effective tactic [4]. Everyone must practice social distancing to prevent a tidal wave of cases, as it is currently the only tool available to fight the spread of the coronavirus [4]. Experts estimate that a vaccine is 12 to 18 months away, and there are no drugs available that can slow down a coronavirus infection [4]. Therefore, slowing or stopping the spread of the virus and decreasing the number of cases at any one time is essential to ensure hospital-level care is available to those who need it [4]. In summary, social distancing is a critical measure to control the spread of COVID-19 by reducing contact between individuals, thereby slowing the transmission rate and preventing healthcare systems from being overwhelmed [4].
